Subject: Nexus AI - inference fit assessment and deployment sketch

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from Redwood's side and the high-level sketch we discussed so we have alignment before we surface an engagement proposal. I’ve kept action items at the bottom.

Key pain / goals you reiterated:
- Latency sensitivity on user-facing completions (search ranker + inline assistant) — target p95 end-to-end client-visible latency <= 200 ms for short prompts (~50-150 tokens).
- High sustained throughput during morning and evening peaks — estimated 1200 QPM (queries per minute) for the assistant use-case with mixed prompt lengths.
- Cost predictability for budgeting (want to avoid burst billing surprises).
- Data isolation & audit for PII (Nexus legal requires HSM/KMS control and 90-day audit log retention).

Model and inference constraints we heard:
- Primary model family: internal preference for open foundation models compatible with instruction tuning (we discussed Llama-3 family and narrow-domain fine-tune).
- Typical prompt + response budget: 512 token context avg, occasionally up to 2k for long-form.
- Need for deterministic reranker outputs for A/B evals — reproducibility across model versions matters.

Suggested SLO / topology options (initial sketch):
1) Dedicated pool (recommended for throughput predictability):
   - Dedicated GPU fleet (reserved nodes) with autoscale headroom for 20% burst.
   - Primary model: quantized 70B (fp16->8-bit quant) for cost/latency tradeoff; fallback to a 13B variant for extreme burst shedding.
   - Latency path: per-request KV cache + prefix caching for frequent prompt patterns; target p95 generation latency < 160 ms on node-local inference for short completions.
2) Hybrid control-plane (private data controls):
   - Private VPC peering + customer KMS for keys; audit logs forwarded to Nexus SIEM.
3) Canary rollout plan:
   - Start with 10% traffic on Dedicated (canary), compare quality & latency to hosted baseline; automatic fallback to hosted if errors spike.

Operational considerations we flagged:
- Batch sizing: dynamic batching tuned to keep p95 within SLA while increasing token throughput; expect average effective batching factor 3–6 depending on concurrency.
- Cache warmup: recommend synthetic traffic warmup and an initial seeding of prefix cache for top-200 prompt patterns.
- Monitoring: token-level cost breakdown, model drift alerts tied to eval prompt sets.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a short worksheet with the numbers you gave (nexus-inference-requirements.xlsx) plus a rough deployment sketch (deployment-sketch.drawio) and a draft cost estimate PDF.

Next steps / asks:
- Alex: confirm the monthly QPM peak we should budget for (you suggested ~1200; confirm if 1500 is safer).
- Nexus security: send the KMS/HSM control spec we need to meet (SAML / SCIM SSO details are useful too).
- Redwood: we’ll produce a 1-page dedicated vs hosted tradeoff + a draft SOW and two capacity options (baseline and high-availability).

Proposed short sync: Thu Jul 1, 09:00 PT to review draft SOW; I’ll send a calendar invite when you confirm.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan

Thanks Priya — solid recap and exactly what we needed. A few clarifications from our side:

1) QPM: 1200 is a safe baseline but plan for a 25% buffer — we’ll confirm 1500 by EOD. That buffer accounts for a planned marketing push in August.
2) Latency: the 200 ms p95 is measured client-visible (includes network hop to our edge), so your internal node p95 target of ~160 ms makes sense.
3) Model family: we are leaning toward Llama-3 70B quantized but want to validate output quality vs a 34B fine-tune for multi-turn coherence on support dialogs. If Redwood can run a quick A/B with our eval set during the canary, that would be ideal.

Samantha will follow up with the KMS/HSM spec this afternoon (she’s copying it to this thread).

Appreciate the SOW draft — please include an itemized line for cache warmup and a separate line for initial synthetic load testing.

Alex

Alex / Priya — quick technical notes based on the numbers above:

- For 1500 QPM with mixed prompt sizes (avg 512 tokens), we should size the dedicated pool for sustained token throughput rather than raw request QPS. Ballpark: 12–16 A100-equivalent instances for the 70B quant pipeline with dynamic batching and KV cache enabled. I’ll include a more precise sim in the cost draft.
- If Nexus requires deterministic reranker outputs across versions, we should pin seed + sampling flags in the rollout and keep a replayable request log for regression tests. That adds ~5% storage/ingest cost but is straightforward.
- Long-context (2k token) paths should use a separate execution class to avoid polluting short-run latency queues; recommend reserving a small fraction (~10%) of capacity for long-form workers.

I’ll attach a quick simulation table in the SOW doc.

—Karthik
